goal: Let the user see a page's title and the actions for all of it
how: A .page-head first in .page: the h1 and one line of purpose in .page-head-text, the actions for the whole page in .page-head-actions with the primary last. --fold turns the actions into one menu by the head's own width, keeping the .actions-keep primary beside it.
avoid: Putting a list's own filters and actions in the page head: they belong in the toolbar above the list.

goal: Let the user read and copy a command or a payload exactly
how: A .code-block around a pre, a .code-block-copy button with data-copy-target, and a .code-block-head naming the file when there is one. A long block is --clamped with a button that shows the rest; several files are tabs in a card.
avoid: Wrapping long lines: the block scrolls sideways so a command copies, and reads, exactly as it runs.

goal: Let the user notice a note, a tip or a caveat written into the content
how: A .callout with an icon and a .callout-body, a .callout-title for its first words, and a tone only where the note is a caveat or a hazard. It is permanent and about the content, so it stays where it is written.
avoid: Using a callout for the state of the page right now, which is an alert, or a page of coloured callouts nobody reads.

goal: Let the user jump between the sections of a long page
how: A nav.page-toc of bare fragment links to the section headings in the sticky aside of a .sedna-split; data-spy marks the section in view aria-current="location", and .page-toc-fold lets the reader fold it once it stacks above the content.
avoid: Contents for a page that fits on a screen or two, where the headings already show the reader everything.

goal: Let the user get back to the top of a long page in one press
how: An a.back-to-top to #top as the last thing in the page, with an aria-label; it sticks to the bottom corner once the page has scrolled a screen down, and moves focus to the top as well as the view.
avoid: A button that only scrolls: the next Tab then lands back at the bottom of the page.

goal: Let the user read one record's fields together in one place
how: A .card with the record's name in .card-head and its state in .card-head-right, and a .kv row per field in the body: values that are figures or ids in the monospace column, prose with .kv--text. .card-section divides the body where the fields fall into groups.
avoid: A table of one row, or a card in a card only to group fields: a card in a card is an object inside an object.

goal: Let the user read a record but claim or unlock it before acting on it
how: A .guard over a card with position: relative, its .guard-card saying why in one sentence and holding the one button that lifts it; the content behind is inert, so it is read but not reached.
avoid: Leaving inert off the guarded content, which keeps every control behind the scrim in the tab order.

goal: Let the user take in a dashboard of panels at a glance
how: A .sedna-grid-24 with a .stat-row across the top, then spans of .sedna-stack columns of cards, so a panel growing in one column moves nothing in the other. It collapses by its own width, with no breakpoint chosen.
avoid: One row of panels of very different heights, which leaves holes beside the short ones: stack each column, span the tall panel, or fix the rows.

goal: Let the user rearrange, resize and fold the panels of their dashboard
how: A .drag-grid of .card--resizable panels: a drop arrives as sedna-drop and a resize as sedna-resize, and the app moves the panel in its own list, keeps its height and its fold per reader, and renders them back.
avoid: Keeping the arrangement only in the page: the next visit starts from the default unless the app stores it per reader.

goal: Let the user keep a side panel in view beside the main content
how: A .sedna-split with the aside marked .sedna-split-aside, first or last in the markup for the side it sits on. The two stack on their own when the main column would get too narrow; --sticky keeps the aside in view and a .split-resize handle lets the reader set its width.
avoid: Choosing a breakpoint for the stack: the split decides by its own width, so the same markup works in a page and in a drawer.

goal: Let the user pick an item from a list and open it
how: A ul.list whose rows are a.list-row to open a record or button.list-row to act, each a .list-title with a .list-sub under it and the state in .list-meta. --cards turns the same markup into separate cards for a work list.
avoid: A click handler on the li: the row is a link or a button, or it has no focus, no keyboard and no announcement.

goal: Let the user scan a long list in groups whose headings stay in view
how: A .sticky-group-head li before each group with --group-head-index counting from 0, so each header pins below the one above it; a .sticky-group-toggle folds a group and .sticky-group-count keeps its count in the head.
avoid: A heading element between two lists: the groups stay one list, or the headers cannot stack.

goal: Let the user see which step of a process they are on and how many are left
how: An ol.steps of short names, each li with data-state done or current and the rest left plain; the numbers come from a CSS counter, so a step added is no renumbering.
avoid: Steps for a record with no end, which is a timeline: the reader can only be on a step of something that finishes.

goal: Let the user open detail only when they want it, one section at a time
how: A .accordion of details elements, each summary an icon and a short label and its content in .accordion-body; the same name on every details makes opening one close the others.
avoid: Hiding what most readers need behind a fold: an accordion is for detail few of them open.

goal: Let the user walk a hierarchy and pick an item from it
how: A ul.tree of role="treeitem" items, each a .tree-row with a .tree-toggle first and a role="group" of children for a branch. The script keeps one tab stop, the arrow keys and typeahead, and writes aria-expanded and aria-selected as the reader works it.
avoid: Leaving aria-selected off an item meant to be picked: without it the item is a heading the reader opens, not a choice.

goal: Let the user tick whole branches of a hierarchy at once
how: aria-checked on every item and a .tree-check in each row: ticking a branch ticks everything under it and makes each parent ticked, unticked or mixed, and sedna-tree-check carries every ticked value for the app to keep.
avoid: Putting an input checkbox in each row, which makes a second tab stop inside every item.

goal: Let the user read what happened to a record and when
how: A ul.timeline of entries, each a .timeline-when and a .timeline-what, newest first, with data-kind only on an entry that mattered; .timeline-group breaks it by day and .timeline-more ends it with the way to earlier entries.
avoid: Colouring every entry: a tone on each one marks none of them.

goal: Let the user switch between views of the same thing without leaving the page
how: A .tabs with role="tablist" and data-tabs, each tab a button with aria-selected and aria-controls naming its tab-panel; the script does the clicks, the arrow keys and the roving tabindex. Where each tab has its own address, the strip is a nav of links instead.
avoid: Using tabs to change a setting, which is a segmented control, or for sections the reader reads one after another.
